work_scope.workstream: Rendered reply debug and copy boundaries
work_scope.authority_owner: Existing rendered reply and backend turn checks
work_scope.required_evidence: Before/after missing-ID pipeline tests; existing console and copy suites; scoped compiler
work_scope.explicit_non_goals: No provider, room, game, backend fetch or installed acceptance changes

review: Runtime fix 51 treats a null or omitted backend turn ID as ineligible instead of calling trim on it. Reply-local identity and backend identity remain separate; no backend identity or fetch is invented.

Six regression/guard tests use real DOM buttons and the actual rendered-reply export pipeline. Two missing-ID cases fail on the original source. Empty IDs, a backend ID absent from button scope, a button ID without matching diagnostics, and detached ancestor traversal remain covered.

The first test run also found an incorrect empty-ID expectation in the new test. Corrected it before editing production; both original and corrected before receipts are retained. The existing empty-backend behavior remains null with a separate local client ID.

The copy formatter already coerces unknown titles/bodies and filters citation strings. Its input type now describes that tolerant existing behavior, without changing emitted JavaScript or the shared response envelope contract.

Legacy reply ID accepts the null already produced by rendered replies. Ancestor traversal uses optional parent access to make its existing terminating null state explicit. Existing console and envelope-copy tests are unchanged.
All three existing production files selected here previously matched the public preview after newline normalization. No private runtime bytes beyond the reviewed patch and test are newly copied.
limits: Unfrozen, unpublished and uninstalled. Mocked envelope serialization and DOM tests do not establish native clipboard, actual backend fetch, or UI acceptance.
Full client typecheck still contains unrelated errors; existing shader/dataset/metadata holds remain.
